verdict: Alexandria took a $638M impairment on properties it plans to sell, driving a $599M net loss; rental revenue fell 11% as it shrinks the portfolio, though funds from operations of $1.54 a share held up.

kpis.label: Total revenues
kpis.note: -11% vs a year ago as assets are sold

kpis.label: FFO per share (as adjusted)
kpis.note: The cash-rent measure REIT investors watch

kpis.label: Impairment charge
kpis.note: On real estate held for sale — non-cash

segments.name: Income from rentals
segments.note: Rent from laboratory and office campuses leased to life-science and technology tenants, mostly in Boston, San Francisco, San Diego and Seattle.

opex.name: Impairment of real estate
opex.note: Writing down properties classified as held for sale to their expected selling prices — a non-cash charge, and the story of this quarter.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of buildings over their lives — non-cash, and added back in the FFO measure.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $80M, partly offset by $24M of investment income, plus a $3M loss on early repayment of debt.

takeaways.title: A write-down quarter
takeaways.text: Alexandria marked down properties it intends to sell by $638M, the main reason for the $599M net loss. As a REIT it pays little income tax, so the loss flows straight through.

takeaways.title: Revenue fell to $671M
takeaways.text: Rent declined as the company sells campuses and life-science leasing demand stays soft — a deliberate shrink to cut debt.

takeaways.title: FFO per share held up
takeaways.text: Funds from operations — which add back depreciation and the impairment — were $1.54 a share on an as-adjusted basis, down from $2.22 a year ago.

footerNote: As a REIT, Alexandria pays essentially no corporate income tax, so no tax line appears. Net loss attributable to common stockholders was $638M, after $39M of income attributable to noncontrolling interests. Figures are from the company's third-quarter 2026 supplemental package filed with the SEC.
